spring:
thaw in the canal —
an axolotl smiles up
at my muddy feet

cherry petals sink
the axolotl wears one
like a small pink hat

spring rain on the pond
feathery gills open
one by one

I wave at the axolotl
it waves back...
with a brand new hand
summer:
hot afternoon —
the axolotl and I
both stay in the shade

summer storm
under the lily pad
a pink grin waits it out

long evening
the axolotl yawns
so I yawn too

cool mud
between my toes —
axolotl country
autumn:
fog on the lake
somewhere below
a smile I can't see

a maple leaf drifts down
the axolotl
nibbles its shadow

harvest moon
floating in the canal —
an axolotl swims through

autumn wind
I hold my breath like an axolotl
... nope
winter:
thin ice
beneath it a pink smile
slow as snow

first frost on the reeds
the axolotl
doesn't mind at all

long night —
an axolotl dreams
at the bottom of the lake

snowflake on my nose
the axolotl
has no nose to catch one

spring:
plum blossom —
a bee and I
reach it at the same time

after the rain
a bee dries its wings
on top of my head

dandelion field
one bee
humming the way home

spring wind
the bee lands on a petal
that just flew off
summer:
heat shimmer
the buzz of the bees
thick as honey

clover in the lawn
I follow a bee
and fall over

thunder far off
bees pour back
into the hive

long evening —
the last bee
hums the sun down
autumn:
late asters
a slow bee
with yellow knees

fallen apple
a bee and a wasp
share without talking

morning mist
the hive door
quiet as a pocket

cold morning —
a bee rests on my paw
we warm each other
winter:
snow on the hive
inside, a hum
like a sleeping kettle

winter sun
one bee steps out
and thinks again

frost on the window
I draw a flower
for the bees

long night
the hive keeps
a summer inside

spring:
spring rain
the cat watches it
from inside my box

cherry petals
a cat swats one
misses, swats me

warm doorstep
the cat and the snowdrops
both wake up

nest in the hedge —
the cat pretends
not to look
summer:
midday heat
the cat pours itself
into the shade

cicadas
the cat's tail
twitching in time

short night
a cat on the fence
counting fireflies

sun patch on the floor
I nap like a cat
and snore like a dog
autumn:
falling leaves
the cat attacks
the loudest one

fog morning
two green eyes
under the porch

harvest moon
a cat on the roof
watching it rise

cold nose —
the cat lets me share
the radiator
winter:
first snow
the cat lifts each paw
like a question

long night
the cat's purr
fills the whole room

frost on the glass
a cat and I
breathe two clouds

I made a snowball
for the cat —
the cat left

spring:
spring mud
the dog comes home
wearing most of it

plum blossom —
the old dog sniffs
each one twice

puddles everywhere
a dog's paw prints
filling with sky

swallows return
the dog barks once
to say hello
summer:
dog days —
even my shadow
is panting

thunder
the big dog hides
behind me

long evening
a stick thrown
into the sunset

garden sprinkler
the dog bites the water
and wins
autumn:
leaf pile
the dog jumps in
and doesn't come out

morning fog
a bark
with no dog yet

harvest moon
the farm dog
howls it higher

wind in the chimney
the dog and I
both lift an ear
winter:
fresh snow
the dog writes
its name everywhere

deep snowdrift —
only a tail
wagging

long night
the sled dogs dream
with running feet

frozen breath
a dog's warm side
is my whole world

spring:
first rains
elephants lift their trunks
to drink the sky

blossoms on the path
the elephant steps
around each one

a new calf
trips on its trunk
like I trip on my feet

spring river
an elephant's spray
becomes a rainbow
summer:
dry season heat
an elephant's ear
fans the whole valley

mud bath —
I tried it too
now I am an elephant

long dusk
the herd walks
into the orange dust

waterhole at noon
elephant footprints
full of tiny frogs
autumn:
the rains move on
an elephant's footprint
holds a small moon

misty morning
something big
rumbles from the ground

ripe marula fruit
the elephant
sways home sleepy

windy grass
an elephant's tail
pointing the way
winter:
cool season
the old elephant
remembers every well

frost on the savanna
an elephant's breath
a small cloud

long night —
I sleep in the shade
of one elephant ear

cold dawn
the herd presses close
I press closer

spring:
old pond —
I jump in too
splash, but louder

spring rain
every puddle
has its own frog

frogspawn
a hundred black dots
looking at me

warm night
the frogs begin
the pond grows wider
summer:
heat haze
a frog on a lily pad
holding very still

after the storm
the frogs sing louder
than the thunder did

long evening
I croak at a frog
it forgives me

cool stone
a frog and I
sharing the shade
autumn:
falling leaf
the frog ducks
a second too late

fog on the pond
one frog
calls the season down

harvest moon
in the ditch
a frog sits inside it

cold rain
the frog's song
shorter every night
winter:
frozen pond
under the ice
a frog dreams of flies

first snow
no frogs tonight —
I croak alone

long night
the mud keeps
a frog warm

frost on the reeds
where the frog sat
a small round melt

spring:
geese return
the whole sky
pointing north

thaw on the river
geese ride down
on the ice

goslings
in a crooked line —
I join the end

spring rain
a goose shakes off
one silver drop at a time
summer:
hot pond
the goose dips its neck
all the way in

long evening
geese still talking
long after dark

summer storm
the gander spreads his wings
over everyone

a goose hissed at me
I hissed back
we both left
autumn:
geese leaving —
the V
wobbles, then holds

fog over the field
only the honking
flies south

harvest moon
one goose crosses it
then another

falling leaves
I flap my arms
nobody follows
winter:
empty sky
somewhere south
my geese are warm

frozen lake
a goose on one leg
then the other

long night
a goose feather
in my pillow dreams

first snow
the last goose
still deciding

spring:
spring dusk
a hedgehog sniffs out
the first slug

blossom petals
stuck on a hedgehog
like small flags

warm rain
the hedgehog wakes up
grumpy and hungry

new leaves
under the hedge
a small snore
summer:
short night
a hedgehog's footsteps
louder than mine

hot day
the hedgehog naps
in a ball of shade

thunder —
the hedgehog
becomes a chestnut

long evening
the hedgehog snuffles
through the clover
autumn:
fallen leaves
the hedgehog wears
half of them

misty garden
a trail of tiny prints
to the woodpile

chestnut on the path
I said hello —
it was a chestnut

harvest moon
the hedgehog eats
for two seasons
winter:
first frost
under the leaf pile
a slow heartbeat

snow on the hedge
somewhere inside
a dream of beetles

long night
I curl up like a hedgehog
but less pointy

thaw drip
the hedgehog turns over
not yet

spring:
first warm rock
the iguana and I
close our eyes

flowering tree
an iguana chews
the pinkest bloom

rainy season begins
the iguana's crest
holding raindrops

I bowed to the iguana
it nodded back
three times
summer:
noon heat
the iguana
turns a deeper green

long afternoon
an iguana on the wall
not moving, not moving

summer storm
the iguana dives
from branch to river

hot sand —
I dance
the iguana doesn't
autumn:
cooler mornings
the iguana waits
for the sun to find it

mango season ends
the iguana checks
the empty branch again

harvest moon
an iguana's eye
half open

windy palms
the iguana holds on
with all of its toes
winter:
cold snap
the iguana dozes off
and slides off the branch

dry season
the iguana and the stone
the same color

long night
the iguana dreams
of warm rocks

cool dawn
I lend the iguana
my sunbeam

spring:
spring tide —
a jellyfish drifts past
my wet toes

april rain
on the harbor... one jellyfish
opens and closes

low tide
I poke a jellyfish
it pokes back, sort of

warm current
the first jellyfish
carries a petal
summer:
heat haze —
a jellyfish lantern
under the pier

beach towel
I mistake a jellyfish
for a lost jelly bean

summer night
the jellyfish glow
where the stars should be

thunder far out
the jellyfish pulse
slower, then slower
autumn:
autumn sea
a jellyfish holds
one red leaf

fog on the bay —
only the jellyfish
know where they go

harvest moon
floating face down
a pale jellyfish

cold wind
I tuck myself in
like a jellyfish
winter:
winter harbor
a jellyfish sleeps
below the thin ice

short day —
the jellyfish and I
both see-through

snow falling
into the dark sea
where jellyfish wait

my breath
fogs the aquarium glass —
the jellyfish vanishes

spring:
eucalyptus buds —
a koala chews
with its eyes closed

spring rain
the koala does not
move one bit

new leaves
I climb halfway up
and nap like a koala

warm morning
a baby koala peeks
from the pouch
summer:
heat wave
a koala hugs
the coolest tree

cicadas —
the koala sleeps
through all of it

long evening
a koala's ear
turned toward the creek

too hot
I hug a lamppost
koala-style
autumn:
autumn gum tree
the koala shifts
to the sunny side

mist in the valley
only a koala's nose
above it

falling bark
the koala grumbles
and keeps chewing

harvest moon
a koala's round shape
in the fork of a branch
winter:
cold night
the koala curls
into its own fur

frost on the leaves
a koala chews
slower than ever

winter rain
I share a branch
with a damp koala

short day —
the koala wakes
just to sleep again

spring:
thaw in the hills
a llama's breath
smells of new grass

spring wind
the llama's ears
turn first

wildflowers —
the llama eats
the one I picked

mountain rain
llamas stand still
in a wet row
summer:
summer pasture
a llama hums
at nothing in particular

heat —
the llama's shadow
is my umbrella

freshly sheared
the llama looks
surprised all day

thunder in the pass
the llamas pull
into a circle
autumn:
first frost
the llama's wool
full of seeds

fog on the trail —
a llama's long neck
appears before the rest

dry leaves
a llama steps around
my small pile

harvest moon
I ask the llama
for directions
winter:
snow on the ridge
a llama's eyelashes
white at the tips

long night
the llama folds
its legs beneath it

winter morning
steam from the llama
steam from me

icy path —
I follow the llama's
sure feet

spring:
spring dusk
a moth wakes up
on the window frame

plum blossom
the moth's wings
the same pale dust

first warm night
a moth and I
both find the porch light

rain on the screen
a moth waits
upside down
summer:
summer night
moths circle the lamp —
I circle too

heat lightning
a moth lands
on my nose

long evening
the moth reads
the lit page with its feet

cicadas fade
the night shift
of moths begins
autumn:
autumn wind
a moth tucked
in a curled leaf

harvest moon
the moth flies straight up
and gives up

mist on the field
the moth's grey wings
made of it

old sweater
a moth hole
shaped like a star
winter:
winter window
a moth asleep
behind the curtain

snowflakes —
for a moment I think
they are moths

long night
one moth
and one candle

frost on the glass
a moth's dusty print
from summer

spring:
ice breaking up
a narwhal's tusk
pokes through

spring light
all night long —
narwhals don't sleep either

melt water
the narwhal points
the way north

first open sea
a pod of narwhals
breathing out loud
summer:
midnight sun
a narwhal's back
shining like wet stone

calm arctic sea
the narwhal's tusk
stirs the clouds

summer swim
I try a tusk
made from a carrot

long day
the narwhals sing
under my feet
autumn:
autumn dusk
the narwhals turn
toward deeper water

sea fog —
only the tusk
and then nothing

first dark night
the narwhal's spiral
counts the stars

cold wind
I point my nose
like a narwhal
winter:
polar night
the narwhal finds
a crack of air

under the ice
a narwhal hums
the whole winter

northern lights —
a narwhal's tusk
green at the tip

snow on the floe
I leave tracks
the narwhal can't

spring:
spring night
an owl's question
answered by frogs

nesting season
the owl's eyes
in a hollow birch

thaw —
owl pellets
in the soft mud

april moon
I hoot once
the owl looks away
summer:
short summer night
the owl starts work
late

heat lingering
the owl turns its head
all the way around

after the storm
a wet owl
shakes like a broom

dusk in the barn
the owl and I
both very still
autumn:
autumn moon
the owl's call
closer this time

falling leaves —
one of them
is an owl

fog at dawn
an owl's white face
in the white

autumn wind
I turn my head like the owl
and fall over
winter:
snowy owl
hard to see
on the snow

long night
the owl counts
something I can't hear

frost on the fence
an owl's footprints
lead nowhere

winter stars
the owl's eyes
two more

spring:
spring rain
a pigeon shakes off
on the bus stop roof

cherry petals
on the sidewalk —
a pigeon pecks one

warm bench
a pigeon and I
split a crumb

spring puddle
the pigeon walks through
twice
summer:
heat on the square
pigeons bathe
in the fountain

summer evening
a pigeon nods
at every step

ice cream cone
the pigeon sees it
before I do

thunder
all the pigeons
lift at once
autumn:
autumn leaves
a pigeon kicks
through the gutter

foggy station
a pigeon waits
for no train

chestnuts roasting —
the pigeons gather
just in case

windy corner
a pigeon walks
backward a little
winter:
first snow
a pigeon's footprints
across the bench

cold morning
pigeons puffed up
like bread rolls

steam from a vent
three pigeons
sharing it

short day
the pigeon and I
head home early

spring:
spring grass
a quokka smiles
with its mouth full

rain shower
the quokka hops
into my shadow

new leaves
a quokka climbs
half a shrub

spring sun
I smile back at the quokka
for too long
summer:
hot sand
a quokka naps
under the bush

salt wind
the quokka's ears
catch it first

summer picnic
the quokka inspects
my sandwich

long evening
quokkas come out
one by one
autumn:
autumn island
a quokka's footprints
in the dew

fallen seeds
the quokka chews
and thinks

harvest moon
a quokka sitting up
to look

autumn drizzle
the quokka still smiling
me less so
winter:
winter rain
a quokka curled
in the hollow

cold dawn
the quokka's breath
and mine

short day
the quokka grazes
faster

grey winter sea
one brown quokka
holding the island down

spring:
spring meadow
a rabbit's ears
above the clover

thaw —
rabbit tracks
turn into mud tracks

dandelions
the rabbit and I
eat the same one

warm rain
a rabbit sits
perfectly round
summer:
summer dusk
the rabbits come out
to the lawn edge

heat —
a rabbit stretched flat
in the shade

storm coming
the rabbit's nose
goes faster

I try to hop
like the rabbit —
summer grass in my mouth
autumn:
harvest moon
I look for the rabbit
in it

fallen apples
a rabbit nibbles
the sweet side

morning fog
a white tail
then only fog

dry leaves
the rabbit freezes
so do I
winter:
fresh snow
rabbit tracks
like little exclamation marks

frosty garden
a rabbit's breath
by the cabbage stalk

long night
the rabbit dreams
of clover, probably

white field
the rabbit's ears
give it away

spring:
after the thaw
a snail and I
share one wet stone

plum petals
the snail wears one
all the way home

spring rain —
i follow a snail's
silver road

racing the snail
to the first dandelion
we both lose
summer:
midday heat
the snail sealed shut
so am I

thunder far off
a snail lifts both horns
to listen

long evening —
the snail halfway
up the flowerpot

I lick the dew
off a lettuce leaf —
the snail looks hurt
autumn:
fallen leaves
a snail climbs
the tallest one

morning fog
only the snail
knows the way

harvest moon
the snail's shell holds
a little of it

I knock on the shell
no one home…
autumn wind
winter:
first frost
the snail's door
sealed with white

snow on the wall
somewhere inside
a snail sleeps

long night
i curl up
like a snail

my breath
fogs the snail shell —
sorry, sorry

spring:
warm stone
a turtle opens
one eye

spring river
the turtle carries
a petal on its back

first rain
the turtle and I
stick our heads out

I sit on a turtle
it takes me
nowhere at all
summer:
noon heat
the turtle wears
the pond

sand still warm
little turtles
follow the moon

cicadas
a turtle naps
on a turtle

too hot —
i try to hide
inside my own back
autumn:
pond mist
the turtle's head
a small island

maple leaves
slide off the shell
one by one

geese leaving
the turtle stays
and stays

harvest moon
the turtle and I
both very round
winter:
ice on the pond
under it
a turtle dreams

cold mud
the turtle's heart
almost still

snowfall
the turtle's shell
wears a hat

long night —
how many winters
in that shell

spring:
spring tide
an urchin rolls
one step closer

rock pool
the urchin and I
watch a crab

warm shallows
an urchin wears
a snail shell

I pet the urchin
it pets me back —
ouch
summer:
low tide
a purple urchin
keeps its spines wet

summer sea
the urchin chews
kelp all day

fireworks —
an urchin
would understand

barefoot on the rocks
i say hello
very carefully
autumn:
storm swell
the urchin holds on
with a hundred feet

autumn moon
in the tide pool
a round urchin

cold current
the kelp thins
the urchin waits

chestnut burr —
for a moment
i say hello to it
winter:
winter sea
an urchin
in a bowl of foam

long night
the urchin's spines
point at every star

frost on the jetty
below the water
a small sun

I try to hug
the urchin
for warmth

spring:
melting snow
a vole's tunnel
opens to the sky

clover
a vole and I
split one leaf

spring rain
the vole's nose
in a dewdrop

I follow the vole
into its hole
most of me fits
summer:
tall grass
somewhere a vole
moves the whole meadow

heat haze
a vole sits up
to count clouds

after the storm
a vole shakes out
its small coat

I nibble a seed
the vole nibbles me
we are even
autumn:
stubble field
a vole carries
one whole grain

first frost on the grass
the vole's pantry
full to the door

owl overhead
the vole and I
are leaves

harvest moon
the vole thinks
it's cheese
winter:
under the snow
a vole's road
goes everywhere

white field
the smallest footprints
are the vole's

long night
the vole's nest
warm with grass

deep snow
only my ears show —
the vole waves

spring:
spring sea
a whale's back
like a new island

thawing coast
the whales
going north again

plankton bloom
the whale opens
its huge mouth

I wave at the whale
the whale
waves the ocean
summer:
long evening
a whale's spout
turns pink

summer stars
a whale breathes
far out

heat on the pier
somewhere below
a whale sings

my belly
and the whale's belly —
both rumble
autumn:
autumn wind
the whale's tail
waves goodbye

harvest moon
a whale rises
right through it

sea fog
only the whale's breath
moves

I try to sing
like the whale —
a pigeon answers
winter:
grey sea
the whales
going south

long night
a whale song
deeper than the cold

ice floes
a whale's back
smooth as snow

frost on my nose
the whale
doesn't even notice

spring:
first rains
a xerus stands up
to smell them

new grass
the xerus nibbles
a green tip

warm dawn
four xerus
at one hole

I try the tail umbrella
my tail
is too short
summer:
noon sun
the xerus
under its own tail

heat shimmer
a xerus
flickers in and out

thunderheads
the xerus dives
into the ground

dust bath
the xerus and I
sneeze together
autumn:
dry grass
a xerus
the same color

harvest moon
over the savanna
one xerus awake

seeds falling
the xerus
fills both cheeks

I dig a burrow
like the xerus —
it's just a dent
winter:
cold dawn
the xerus waits
for the sun

long night
the xerus family
in one heap

frost on the acacia
a xerus
fluffs its tail

my breath, its breath
two small clouds
nose to nose

spring:
mountain thaw
a yak calf
on wobbly legs

prayer flags snapping
the yak
chews and chews

spring snowmelt
the yak's beard
dripping

I ride the yak
for three steps —
now I ride the grass
summer:
high meadow
the yak sheds
its winter coat

summer storm
yaks standing
like hills

long evening
the yak's shadow
crosses the valley

yak fluff
i wear it
as a cloud
autumn:
first snow on the peaks
the yaks
come down

geese overhead
the yak
does not look up

harvest moon
on the long horns
a little light

autumn wind
i hide
in the yak's long hair
winter:
blizzard
the yak
faces into it

frozen beard
the yak's breath
a small cloud

long night
under the yak
warm enough

snow on the yak
snow on me —
who is the yak now

spring:
first rains
zebra foals
all legs

new grass
the zebras' stripes
brighter

river crossing
a zebra shakes
the water off

I count the stripes
lose count
start again
summer:
noon heat
zebras rest
head to tail

heat haze
the herd becomes
one striped cloud

dry thunder
the zebra's ears
turn

I paint stripes on
with mud —
nobody is fooled
autumn:
dry season
the zebras walk
toward the rain

dusty wind
a zebra
blinks it away

harvest moon
zebra stripes
moonlight stripes

a zebra yawns
i yawn
the whole herd yawns
winter:
cold night
zebras pressed
side by side

frost on the savanna
a zebra's breath
goes white

long night
the stripes
under the stars

black and white
like snow on rock —
but warm
